careerPlanner.title: Don't know what you want yet? Good place to start.
careerPlanner.intro: I'll ask a few short questions, starting with work you've already done. Skip anything you want. You get three directions to look at. You pick one, or you don't. Both are fine.
careerPlanner.canStillAnswer: You can still answer the questions.

liked.prompt: Think about work you've done. Paid, unpaid, side work, helping family. What part felt good?
liked.help: Tap anything below that felt good to do, and add your own words if you want.

goodAt.prompt: What are you good at that nobody ever asked you about?
goodAt.help: Fixing things, calming people down, keeping track of money, cooking for a crowd. Your words, not ours.

proud.prompt: Tell me about one time you did something and went home proud of it. Anything counts.
proud.help: No wrong answers. It doesn't have to be a job.

soon.prompt: How soon do you need money coming in?

options.months: I can take a few months

training.prompt: Would you do training before the first paycheck?

options.none: No, I need to work first
options.long: I'd do longer training for the right thing

transport.prompt: How do you get to work?

options.license_no_car: I have a license but no car

physical.prompt: Anything your body can't do all day?

licensing.prompt: Some jobs need a state license, and licensing rules about records differ by state. Look at those now, or skip them for now?
licensing.help: Only you know if this matters for you. Nobody here is asking about your record.

payFloor.prompt: What's the least an hour you can take?
payFloor.help: Your number. Skip it if you don't know.

employers.title: Employers That Hire People With Records
employers.intro: Employers with published hiring evidence. Checked and reported evidence are labeled separately. Each one shows where we looked and when, and the words we found. Read the notes. Some have honest caveats.
employers.buildingTitle: This database is still being built.
employers.buildingBody: The list is deliberately small: an employer is added only when we find current, dated evidence that it hires people with records, and the mark runs out on its own unless someone confirms it again. A name here means something. If your area is not covered yet, that is not a dead end. Use Job Search for live listings and the disclosure planner to prepare. A missing employer is not a "no."

resourcesPage.hiringCaveat: A company that hires people with records does not approve everyone automatically. Background checks still vary by role, location, timing, and the relationship between the record and the job.
